chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Blessing hastens more to the house from which kindness is sought/obtained, than the blade in the hump of the camel, or the flood to its destination.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of kindness (Ma'ruf) in attracting divine blessing to a home according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to illustrate how active generosity (i'ta') accelerates divine blessing (barakah) into the home, a concept central to Shia ethical teachings on social cohesion. The vivid simile of the blade in the camel's hump or the flood's course underscores the immediacy and inevitability of this spiritual reward, contrasting it with the slow, gradual nature of ordinary sustenance. This narration reinforces the Shia emphasis on 'al-Ma'ruf' (customary good) as a tangible mechanism for repelling calamities and enhancing domestic tranquility.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Blessings come quicker to the house from which the acts of kindness emanate from than the blade in the hump of the camel, or a flood’s moving towards its destination’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated this Hadith. ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Blessings cut through obstacles faster than a knife’s cutting through the hump of a camel or a flood’s moving toward its destination, to reach the house from which Benevolent Assistance is provided.’”
